caveat: Conceptual; no empirical test of the proposed reasoning.
title: Which inference is at risk? Assessment validity reasoning and generative AI
why: Asks which inference an assessment actually licenses once AI is in the loop - a cleaner question than the usual integrity panic, and directly usable in curriculum arguments.
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has unsettled higher education assessment because it changes what student performances can reasonably be taken to mean. This conceptual article further develops a validity-centred account of this disruption, distinguishing several problems that are often collapsed in debate: construct underrepresentation, construct-irrelevant variance, attribution of performance, conditional extrapolation, and unsupported score use. It then proposes a practical reasoning sequence for assessment redesign that begins with specifying the intended claim and the AI conditions, proceeds through threat diagnosis and proportionate design response, and ends with local evidence. A compact Validity Reasoning Matrix illustrates how course and program teams can align concerns, threatened inferences, redesigns, and evidence needs. The contribution is both conceptual and practical: it offers a language for moving beyond detection and generic AI-proofing and a usable structure for defending assessment claims in AI-inclusive higher education.
